title: Double-clicking the ruler outside a selected range clears it
goal: User 2026-09-29: 'when I have a range selected in the scrub bar, and I double click elsewhere on the scrub bar, I want the range cleared.' Range selection shipped with select-a-range-of-time-across-clips-and-tracks-a. Reproduce the current behaviour first (what a double-click outside the range does today).
acceptance: With a range selected, double-clicking the ruler or scrub bar anywhere outside the range clears the range (and its In/Out), and the playhead lands where you double-clicked
A single click outside the range keeps today's behaviour; double-clicking INSIDE the range does not clear it
Escape with the pointer over the timeline, and right-click on the ruler > Clear Range, also clear it (Premiere's Clear In and Out, Opt-X, too)
Clearing is not an undo step of its own unless setting the range was

Walk at Next defaults: drag a range on the ruler, double-click outside it with a pointer click (not an accessibility press), check the range is gone and the playhead moved; double-click inside a new range and check it stays

log.note: Reproduced with a real-pointer walk (Scripts/playtest/double-click-clears-a-range-walk.json, pre-fix): a range just drawn by hand does clear on a double-click beside it, because the first click of the pair already drops a range still in hand. But marks set with I and O (and a drawn range once anything else has been picked) survive a double-click beside them: step 31 FAILED 'there is an In at 3000ms; there is an Out at 5000ms'. The transport's scrub bar never clears marks on any click. Escape does nothing to the marks.

Adversarial review before building: Premiere clears In/Out with Opt-X or the ruler's right-click, Final Cut drops a range on a click beside it; a double-click beside is a gentle superset that never collides with a single click (still Premiere's: marks stay). Risk: Escape is the canvas's deselect key; Escape clears the marks only while the timeline has the keyboard (any press in the dock gives it, the same panel-focus rule every timeline key uses) and only when there are marks, otherwise it carries on to the canvas. Treating keyboard focus as 'pointer over the timeline'.

Root cause: the first click of a double-click moves the playhead under the pointer, so the second press lands ON the playhead and was taken as a scrub. Fixed in the playhead branch plus core rulerClickClearsMarks. Neighbour walks green (draw-a-range x2, captions-and-export-for-a-range, export-keeps-to-the-in-and-out after renaming its row to Clear Range, extract-from-the-ruler-menu, timeline-right-click, play-in-to-out-from-the-ruler, copy-a-range-from-its-menu, the-ninety-second-cut, window-modes, notice-carries-the-way-out). Left rough, no task: Escape follows timeline keyboard focus rather than pointer hover (same as every timeline key); a by-name press on the transport Scrub control does not drive its drag gesture, so the walk uses a pointer windowClick there.

A double-click on the ruler or transport scrub bar outside the marked range clears it (drawn or I/O marks) and moves the playhead there; inside it stays; a single click is unchanged. Escape on a focused timeline and a new Clear Range right-click row (Opt-X) clear it too; clearing is one undo step, as setting was. Commit e2c35cc4. Verified: new core tests + full suite (10,526) green; real-pointer walk double-click-clears-a-range-walk green at Next defaults with 7 real captures; 11 neighbouring walks green.
